# Tools: Workspace executive context

### `get_workspace_executive_context` [A] · read · workspace:read · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns the workspace's merged executive context: mandate, executive role assignments, portfolio policies, delivery and financial settings, and completeness metadata.
Use when: Before drafting or applying an executive context patch, to see current values; To find who holds an executive role (governance.assignments) or which roles are missing (governance.missingRoles); To read priority rules, routing policy summary or curation SLA before triaging or routing intake    Avoid when: You need the canonical ready/not-ready verdict -> generate_workspace_readiness_report; You need the list of gaps with suggested actions -> list_workspace_context_gaps; You need portfolio health, decisions or finance rollups -> get_workspace_owner_surface or get_workspace_read_model
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | On an OAuth connector bound to a single workspace it may be omitted. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member; On OAuth connectors the grant has scope workspace:read
Returns: {workspace{id, name, access.canManage, ...}, executiveContext{version:1, workspaceId, mandate{mission, operatingModel, strategicIntent, successCriteria[]}, governance{assignments[{role, userId, source, assignedAt, assignedBy}], missingRoles[], escalationPolicy, decisionPolicy}, portfolio{domains[], capabilities[], systems[], projectCount, priorityRules[], routingPolicySummary}, delivery{curationSlaHours, releasePolicy, operationalCadence}, financial{currency, hourlyRateDefault, budgetPolicy}, metadata{completenessStatus, completenessScore 0-100, lastReviewedAt, updatedAt}}}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace (also when the workspaceId does not exist) | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| JSON-RPC -32003 | Call get_mcp_connection_info to see which scopes/tools this connection has. |
Gotchas:
- Builds the full workspace read model internally (same server cost as get_workspace_read_model) and returns only the context.
- The 5 executive roles are workspace-owner, portfolio-owner, operations-lead, finance-owner, routing-owner.
- metadata.completenessStatus is a simple field score (>=85 complete, >=50 partial, else blocked) and can disagree with the readiness verdict; use generate_workspace_readiness_report for the verdict.
- portfolio.domains/capabilities/systems are plain strings merged with the project routing profiles; they are NOT the roadmap capability records of list_workspace_capabilities.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `list_workspace_context_gaps`, `draft_workspace_operating_model`, `draft_workspace_routing_policy`

### `list_workspace_context_gaps` [A] · read · KEY · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists every structured gap in the workspace executive context (missing roles, mission, priority/routing policy, currency, unowned domains/capabilities, misaligned project routing profiles) with severity, evidence and a suggested action.
Use when: Diagnosing why the readiness report is blocked or partial; Building a to-do list for the owner to complete the executive context; Choosing which draft to generate (sourceGapIds of the drafts refer to these gap ids)    Avoid when: Only domain/capability ownership and project alignment -> list_unowned_domains_or_capabilities; Only missing executive roles -> list_missing_governance_assignments; You want a status and score verdict -> generate_workspace_readiness_report
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore document ID. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member; API key access: this tool is not exposed to OAuth connectors
Returns: {workspace, executiveContext, generatedAt, items[{id (e.g. 'missing-governance-role:finance-owner', 'unowned-domain:<name>'), workspaceId, gapType missing-governance-role|missing-mandate|missing-priority-policy|missing-routing-policy|missing-financial-context|unowned-domain|unowned-capability|inconsistent-project-alignment, severity low|medium|high|critical, title, detail, evidence[], suggestedAction, requiresHumanConfirmation}]}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| Tool not listed or -32003 on an OAuth connector | This tool needs an LPM API key (x-api-key); call get_mcp_connection_info to confirm what the connection allows. |
Gotchas:
- title, detail and suggestedAction are in Portuguese; evidence is in English.
- Severity: missing workspace-owner or portfolio-owner = critical, other missing roles = high, unowned domain/capability = high, project routing profile pointing to another workspace = critical.
- All gaps except missing mission have requiresHumanConfirmation=true: report them to the owner, do not fix silently.
- Fix map: missing-governance-role -> apply_workspace_context_update governance.assignmentsToAdd (owner approval); missing-mandate -> mandate.mission; missing-priority-policy/missing-routing-policy -> draft_workspace_routing_policy; missing-financial-context -> financial.currency (owner-only) or harmonize project currencies; unowned-domain/capability and inconsistent-project-alignment -> update_project routingProfile.
- items is empty when the context cannot be built.
- Same server cost as get_workspace_read_model.
Pairs with: `get_workspace_executive_context`, `draft_workspace_operating_model`, `draft_workspace_routing_policy`, `apply_workspace_context_update`, `generate_workspace_readiness_report`

### `list_unowned_domains_or_capabilities` [A] · read · KEY · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns only the ownership-coverage gaps: executive-context domains and capabilities that no project claims, plus projects whose routing profile points to another workspace.
Use when: Before routing intake, to see which areas have no owning project; validate_workspace_project_alignment reported warnings or blockers and you need the individual items    Avoid when: All gap types -> list_workspace_context_gaps; Only a status/score for alignment -> validate_workspace_project_alignment; Roadmap capability records (ids, owners, tags) -> list_workspace_capabilities
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore document ID. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member; API key access: not exposed to OAuth connectors
Returns: {workspace, executiveContext, generatedAt, unownedDomains[gap], unownedCapabilities[gap], alignmentIssues[gap]} where each gap is {id, gapType, severity, title, detail, evidence[], suggestedAction, requiresHumanConfirmation} as in list_workspace_context_gaps.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| Tool not listed or -32003 on an OAuth connector | Needs an LPM API key; call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- 'Capabilities' here are executive-context strings matched against project routingProfile.ownedCapabilities, not roadmap capability records.
- A domain or capability counts as owned when at least one non-archived project's routingProfile lists it (routingProfile.domains / routingProfile.ownedCapabilities).
- Fix by claiming it on the right project with update_project routingProfile (confirm with the user), or by removing it from the context with apply_workspace_context_update portfolio.domains/capabilities (owner-only; that list is replaced, not merged).
- Strings that come from a project's routing profile cannot be removed through the context.
- alignmentIssues usually means a project's routingProfile.workspaceId is stale: re-save the routingProfile with update_project.
Pairs with: `list_workspace_projects`, `update_project`, `validate_workspace_project_alignment`

Purpose: Lists workspace executive roles (workspace-owner, portfolio-owner, operations-lead, finance-owner, routing-owner) that have no explicit responsible person.

Returns: {workspace, executiveContext, generatedAt, items[{id:'missing-governance-role:<role>', gapType:'missing-governance-role', severity:'critical' (workspace-owner, portfolio-owner) | 'high', title, detail, evidence[], suggestedAction, requiresHumanConfirmation:true}]}

Purpose: Builds, without saving, a proposed executive-context patch for the workspace operating model: mandate (operating model, strategic intent, success criteria), decision and escalation policies, operational cadence and release policy.
Use when: Readiness shows missing mandate or governance gaps and the owner asked for a proposal; The owner asks how the workspace should operate and wants a starting text to edit    Avoid when: Priority rules, routing policy or curation SLA -> draft_workspace_routing_policy; Assigning executive roles: drafts never assign roles; build a governance.assignmentsToAdd patch with the owner for apply_workspace_context_update; Saving anything -> apply_workspace_context_update (owner-only)
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore document ID. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member; API key access: not exposed to OAuth connectors
Returns: {workspace, executiveContext, generatedAt, draft{draftType:'operating-model', title, summary, rationale[], assumptions[], sourceGapIds[], proposedPatch{workspaceId, reason, patch{mandate{operatingModel, strategicIntent, successCriteria[]}, governance{decisionPolicy, escalationPolicy}, delivery{operationalCadence, releasePolicy}}}, review{sensitivity, requiresHumanConfirmation, touchedAreas[]}, validationIssues[], requiresHumanConfirmation, generatedAt}}. draft is null when the context cannot be built.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |

- Nothing is persisted; safe to call any number of times.

### `apply_workspace_context_update` [O] · write · KEY · profiles: full, portfolio, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: not idempotent: no key; last writer wins; re-read executiveContext.metadata.lastReviewedAt before any retry
Purpose: Writes an owner-approved patch to the workspace executive context (mandate, executive roles, portfolio policies, delivery settings, financial settings) with validation and an audit event.
Use when: The owner approved a specific patch (often draft.proposedPatch from draft_workspace_operating_model or draft_workspace_routing_policy) and asked you to apply it; The owner told you who holds an executive role (portfolio-owner, operations-lead, finance-owner, routing-owner) and asked you to record it    Avoid when: You only want to see a proposal -> draft_workspace_operating_model / draft_workspace_routing_policy; Changing which project owns a domain or capability -> update_project routingProfile; Roadmap items or capability records -> roadmap change tools / create_workspace_capability; The owner has not approved the exact patch: present it and wait
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore document ID. |
| reason | yes | user (or draft.proposedPatch.reason) | Non-empty text; stored in the audit trail. |
| patch | yes | draft_workspace_operating_model / draft_workspace_routing_policy -> draft.proposedPatch.patch, or built from the owner's instructions | Object touching at least one of: mandate{mission, operatingModel, strategicIntent, successCriteria[]}, governance{assignmentsToAdd[{role, userId}], assignmentsToRemove[{role, userId}], assignments[{role, userId}], missingRoles[], escalationPolicy, decisionPolicy}, portfolio{domains[], capabilities[], systems[], priorityRules[], routingPolicySummary}, delivery{curationSlaHours >= 0, releasePolicy, operationalCadence}, financial{currency ISO 4217, hourlyRateDefault >= 0, budgetPolicy}. role enum: workspace-owner\|portfolio-owner\|operations-lead\|finance-owner\|routing-owner. userId from list_workspace_members -> userId. |
| confirmSensitiveChanges | no | constant true, only after the owner explicitly approved this exact patch | Required for sensitive fields (see gotchas); otherwise the call fails. |
| requestedBy | no | list_workspace_members -> userId of the owner who requested it | Defaults to the caller; stored as assignedBy on new role assignments. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an admin member; The owner explicitly approved the exact patch (GOV-MAX); financial fields are always the owner's decision; API key access: not exposed to OAuth connectors
Returns: {workspace, executiveContext (the new stored context), review{sensitivity safe|sensitive, requiresHumanConfirmation, touchedAreas[]}, validationIssues[], changedFields[], auditEventId, appliedAt}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have permission to update this workspace executive context | Caller is not owner/admin. Hand the approved patch to the owner; do not look for another credential. |
| Sensitive workspace executive context changes require human confirmation | Show the patch to the owner; retry with confirmSensitiveChanges=true only after explicit approval. |
| Workspace executive context patch is invalid | Details are not returned over MCP. Check: reason not empty, patch has at least one of mandate/governance/portfolio/delivery/financial, every role is in the enum and every userId is a non-empty string. |
| Workspace executive context <field> must be an array of strings / must be a non-negative number | Send arrays of strings for list fields and numbers >= 0 for curationSlaHours and hourlyRateDefault. |
| Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim') | An assignment is missing role or userId; send both as strings. |
| Workspace executive context not found | Re-check workspaceId with list_workspaces. |
| -32003 This API key is not allowed to call MCP tool | The key's access profile excludes this write tool; ask the owner. Never create or swap keys yourself. |
Gotchas:
- Sensitive (needs confirmSensitiveChanges=true): any governance assignment change, decisionPolicy, escalationPolicy, priorityRules, routingPolicySummary, releasePolicy and any financial field.
- Text and number fields: null does NOT clear a value (keeps the current one, despite the schema note on currency); an empty string clears it, and a derived default may then reappear on read.
- Array fields (successCriteria, domains, capabilities, systems, priorityRules) REPLACE the stored list.
- governance.assignments only upserts by role and never removes; remove with assignmentsToRemove (role AND userId must match the current holder).
- A missing-role blocker clears only by assigning the role; a missingRoles override does not stick.
- userId is not checked against membership.
- Reads may show the old context for about 5 s (read cache).
- Re-run generate_workspace_readiness_report after every apply.
- Each call writes the WHOLE context, computed from a read model that may be up to 5 s old, and appends a new audit event: a concurrent change or two applies in a row can revert fields. Re-read get_workspace_executive_context (metadata.lastReviewedAt) before any retry or second apply.
Pairs with: `draft_workspace_operating_model`, `draft_workspace_routing_policy`, `generate_workspace_readiness_report`, `validate_workspace_project_alignment`

### `validate_workspace_context_completeness` [A] · read · workspace:read · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Checks whether the workspace executive context is complete enough for assisted operation and returns a status, score, blockers, warnings, field issues and next actions.
Use when: Checking only the context side (mandate, roles, policies) before letting agents act more autonomously; After an approved apply_workspace_context_update, to confirm blockers were removed    Avoid when: You want one verdict combining completeness and project alignment -> generate_workspace_readiness_report; Only project ownership drift -> validate_workspace_project_alignment; The individual gap list -> list_workspace_context_gaps
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | On an OAuth connector bound to a single workspace it may be omitted. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member; On OAuth connectors the grant has scope workspace:read
Returns: {workspace, executiveContext, validation{validationType:'context-completeness', status complete|partial|blocked, score 0-100, blockers[gap], warnings[gap], issues[{field, severity, message}], nextActions[] (max 5)}, generatedAt}. validation is null when the context cannot be built.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| JSON-RPC -32003 | Call get_mcp_connection_info to see which scopes/tools this connection has. |
Gotchas:
- Every missing executive role is a blocker, so status stays 'blocked' until all 5 roles are assigned (workspace-owner is derived automatically from the owner membership; the other 4 need explicit assignment via apply_workspace_context_update).
- A missing mission or zero assignments also blocks.
- nextActions are the gaps' Portuguese suggestedAction strings.
- Nothing is stored; same server cost as get_workspace_read_model.
Pairs with: `list_workspace_context_gaps`, `draft_workspace_operating_model`, `apply_workspace_context_update`

### `validate_workspace_project_alignment` [A] · read · workspace:read · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Checks ownership alignment between the executive context and the projects: unowned domains/capabilities (warnings) and project routing profiles pointing to another workspace (blockers).
Use when: Before routing intake or allocating roadmap work, to confirm every domain/capability has an owning project; After changing project routing profiles with update_project    Avoid when: One combined verdict -> generate_workspace_readiness_report; The concrete unowned items -> list_unowned_domains_or_capabilities; Role or mandate completeness -> validate_workspace_context_completeness
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | On an OAuth connector bound to a single workspace it may be omitted. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member; On OAuth connectors the grant has scope workspace:read
Returns: {workspace, executiveContext, validation{validationType:'project-alignment', status complete|partial|blocked, score 0-100, blockers[inconsistent-project-alignment gaps], warnings[unowned-domain / unowned-capability gaps], issues[] (always empty), nextActions[]}, generatedAt}. validation is null when the context cannot be built.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| JSON-RPC -32003 | Call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- Status is 'partial' even with zero alignment problems when the context's completenessStatus is 'partial'.
- Blockers in practice come from a project whose routingProfile.workspaceId differs from this workspace (fix: re-save routingProfile with update_project).

Pairs with: `list_unowned_domains_or_capabilities`, `update_project`, `generate_workspace_readiness_report`

### `generate_workspace_readiness_report` [A] · read · workspace:read · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Computes the canonical readiness verdict for the workspace executive context: combined status, score, blockers, warnings and next actions from the completeness and alignment checks.
Use when: Answering 'is this workspace ready for assisted or agent operation?' or 'what is missing?'; After every approved apply_workspace_context_update (the runbook treats this report as the closure signal); Start of an owner session, to decide what to propose first    Avoid when: You need every gap including details per type -> list_workspace_context_gaps; You need the context values themselves -> get_workspace_executive_context
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | On an OAuth connector bound to a single workspace it may be omitted. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member; On OAuth connectors the grant has scope workspace:read
Returns: {workspace, executiveContext, report{version:1, workspaceId, status complete|partial|blocked, score 0-100 (average of completeness and alignment scores), blockers[gap], warnings[gap], nextActions[] (max 6), generatedAt}, generatedAt}. report is null when the context cannot be built.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| JSON-RPC -32003 | Call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- Despite 'generate', nothing is stored; deterministic, no AI cost.
- A new workspace is normally 'blocked' because 4 executive roles are unassigned.
- blockers = missing roles, critical gaps and misaligned project routing profiles; warnings = the other gaps.
- nextActions are Portuguese text from the gaps.
- Same server cost as get_workspace_read_model.
Pairs with: `list_workspace_context_gaps`, `draft_workspace_operating_model`, `draft_workspace_routing_policy`, `apply_workspace_context_update`

### `list_workspace_members` [A] · read · workspace:read · owner `lpm-workspace-admin` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the members of a workspace with their roles.
Use when: You need the userId, email or role of people in a workspace.; You must confirm the caller is owner/admin before using admin tools.; Choosing accountableOwnerUserId (role owner/admin) for agent principals or credentials.; Before add_workspace_member, to avoid adding someone twice. ### `update_project` [C] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-workspace-admin` · profiles: full, portfolio, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Changes project settings: name, description, archived flag, workspace or team placement, governance role assignments or routing profile.
Use when: User asks to rename the project or edit its description; The owner explicitly instructs to set the project-owner, product-owner or delivery-lead assignments; The owner explicitly instructs to move the project to another workspace or team    Avoid when: Only archiving or restoring: use archive_project or unarchive_project; Changing work items: use update_issue, update_cycle or update_milestone; Changing scope or roadmap: use the governed flows (change sets, submit_workspace_roadmap_change), not project settings
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
| name | no | user | Trimmed; empty string is rejected. |
| description | no | user | Trimmed. |
| archived | no | constant | Boolean. Prefer archive_project / unarchive_project. |
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Moves the project to that workspace and recomputes its routing profile. |
| teamId | no | list_teams -> id | Moves the project to that team. |
| governanceAssignments | no | user (userId from list_project_assignable_members -> uid) | Array of {role: project-owner\|product-owner\|delivery-lead, userId}. REPLACES the whole list; one entry per role; userIds starting with 'agent:' are dropped. |
| routingProfile | no | user | Object of string arrays: domains, ownedCapabilities, ownedComponents, ownedSystems, aliases, intakeKeywords, excludedKeywords, escalationRules, maintainedBy. Requires the project to belong to a workspace. |
Preconditions: Caller can manage the project (project owner, project-owner role, workspace manager or team admin); governanceAssignments, routingProfile and workspace/team moves only on explicit owner instruction, because they change who decides; API key authentication (not offered to OAuth connectors)
Returns: Plain text: 'Project <projectId> updated successfully.' Call get_project to read the new state.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project not found | Wrong projectId; get it from list_projects (includeArchived=true). |
| You do not have permission to update this project | Caller is not a project manager. Stop and tell the user who can do it (get_project -> governanceAssignments). |
| You do not have access to the target workspace / target team | Use a workspace or team the caller belongs to. |
| Project routing profile requires the project to belong to a workspace | Set workspaceId first (owner decision) or drop routingProfile. |
| Hourly rate must be a valid number / Operational curation SLA must be between 1 and 720 hours | You sent an undeclared field; remove it (hourlyRate is a financial decision for the owner). |
Gotchas:
- Every argument except projectId is written into the project document as sent; the server does not reject unknown fields.
- Send ONLY the fields you mean to change and never send fields outside the schema.
- governanceAssignments replaces the full list: read get_project first and resend the roles you keep.
- Records a 'settings updated' activity only when something changed.
Pairs with: `get_project`, `list_project_assignable_members`, `list_workspaces`

### `update_workspace` [C] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-workspace-admin` · profiles: full, portfolio, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Changes a workspace's name, slug, description or status (active or archived).
Use when: The user asks to rename a workspace or change its description.; The user explicitly asks to archive or reactivate a workspace.    Avoid when: You want to change AI providers, models or budgets: that is update_workspace_ai_config (owner-only).; You want to change members: use add_workspace_member or remove_workspace_member.; You want to change the operating model or context: use apply_workspace_context_update.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id |  |
| name | no | user | Non-empty if sent. |
| slug | no | user | Not validated or checked for uniqueness. |
| description | no | user |  |
| status | no | constant | Only 'active' or 'archived' (the server does not validate it with an API key). |
Preconditions: The workspace exists.; The caller is workspace owner or an active member with role owner/admin (list_workspaces -> access.canManage = true).
Returns: Text 'Workspace <workspaceId> updated successfully.' Only the fields you sent change.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'Workspace not found' | Re-read ids with list_workspaces. |
| 'You do not have permission to update this workspace' | Ask the workspace owner or an admin. |
| 'Workspace name is required' | Do not send an empty name. |
Gotchas:
- status='archived' is an archive: ChatGPT/Claude OAuth connectors bound to that workspace start failing with access denied and it disappears from OAuth list_workspaces.
- Treat it as destructive and confirm.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `get_workspace`

### `get_project` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-start` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns one project's settings with its resolved governance roles and whether the caller can manage it.
Use when: Verify a projectId and show its name/key before acting; Find who holds project-owner, product-owner and delivery-lead roles (who to escalate to); Check access.canManage before tools that need manage rights (update_project, archive_project, create_project_file, delete_project_file)    Avoid when: You need open issues, decisions and scope gate: use get_project_execution_context; You need the executive summary only: use get_project_owner_surface; You do not know the projectId yet: use list_projects
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
Preconditions: Caller can read the project; Under OAuth the project must belong to a workspace in the grant
Returns: JSON project: id, name, key, description, ownerId, workspaceId, teamId, archived, createdAt, governanceAssignments [{role, userId, source}] (resolved), routingProfile, plus access {canManage: boolean}.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project <id> not found | Wrong ID; get it from list_projects. |
| You do not have access to this project | Caller cannot read it; ask the user for access, do not retry. |
| -32003 (OAuth) not authorized | Project is outside the granted workspace or has no workspace; call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- Cheap call: one project document read plus a permission check (access.canManage).
- Holding a governance role is authority to decide; being an issue assignee is not.
Pairs with: `list_projects`, `get_project_execution_context`, `update_project`
CLI: `lpm project get <projectId> [--json]`

### `get_workspace_read_model` [A] · read · workspace:read · owner `lpm-review-health` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns the full aggregated workspace read model in one payload: the workspace record, the owner executive summary (ownerView) and the merged executive context.
Use when: You need ownerView and executiveContext together in one call, e.g. for a full executive briefing to the owner; You need per-project executive summaries (ownerView.projects[]) or portfolio risk signals (ownerView.risks[]); You are on an OAuth connector (ChatGPT/Claude) and need the owner dashboard: get_workspace_owner_surface is not available there    Avoid when: You only need the owner dashboard numbers -> get_workspace_owner_surface (same data minus executiveContext, API key only); You only need mandate, roles and policies -> get_workspace_executive_context; You poll repeatedly or need roadmap, repository freshness and code-search budget -> get_workspace_owner_context_bundle with sinceVersion; You need to know what is missing -> generate_workspace_readiness_report or list_workspace_context_gaps
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore document ID. On an OAuth connector bound to a single workspace it may be omitted (the grant's workspace is used). |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member (any role); On OAuth connectors the grant has scope workspace:read and covers this workspace
Returns: {workspace{id, name, ownerId, description, access.canManage, ...}, ownerView{generatedAt, workspace{projectCount, memberCount, ...}, governance{projectsMissingProjectOwner, projectsMissingProductOwner, projectsMissingDeliveryLead}, portfolio{healthStatus healthy|watch|critical, blockedIssuesOpen, overdueIssues, completionRate, throughput30d, projectsWithoutCurrentBaseline}, finance{currency, currencyMode, forecastCost, actualCost, ...}, dependencies, activity, attention{priorityProjectCount, recommendedProject}, decisions{pendingCount, actionRequiredCount, items[]}, copilot{executiveBrief, readyQuestions[]}, projects[], risks[]}, executiveContext{mandate, governance, portfolio, delivery, financial, metadata}}. workspace.access.canManage=true means the caller can use owner/admin write tools.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace (also returned when the workspaceId does not exist) | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE (result over the 1,000,000-byte MCP response cap; nothing is returned) | Use get_workspace_owner_surface or get_workspace_executive_context, or get_workspace_owner_context_bundle with detailLevel=compact. |
| JSON-RPC -32003 (OAuth scope or API-key allow-list denied) | Call get_mcp_connection_info to see granted scopes/tools; on ChatGPT a new scope needs removing and reinstalling the connector and ticking the box. |
Gotchas:
- Heaviest read in this group: it loads every issue, cycle, milestone, baseline, requirement, governance thread, execution and ledger entry of every non-archived project.
- Large workspaces can exceed the 1 MB response cap (error, not truncation). Cached about 5 s per user.
- executiveContext is merged: stored values win, otherwise derived defaults are shown (mission falls back to workspace.description, operatingModel to 'workspace-first', workspace-owner role derived from the owner membership).
- Archived projects are excluded.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `generate_workspace_readiness_report`, `list_workspace_context_gaps`
